A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CollectiveKV. Their complete main text, equations, Tables 1–4, Figures 1–9, and Appendices A–G are readable and matchable despite page reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original recommendation, compression, latency, and ablation results, plus empirical analyses of cross-user similarity, router activations, and long-tail users.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The shared KV pool, user-specific projections, router, training/inference procedures, and peak and balance losses in Section 4 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same recommendation tasks on MicroVideo, KuaiVideo, and EBNeRD-Small, including the same long-tail user evaluation in Appendix G. No dataset or test population is added.

E2.justification: SIM, SDIM, ETA, TWIN, and HSTU retain the same comparisons with their CollectiveKV variants, and Table 2 retains standard KV caching as the latency comparator. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The metrics, latency batch sizes, and analysis procedures are unchanged. Section 5.1 newly attributes splitting and configuration settings to LAIN, but does not revise a previously stated setting or establish that experiments changed.

E4.justification: The dimension and pool-size sensitivity analyses, loss and key/value ablations, router activation analyses, and long-tail evaluation are retained unchanged in Sections 5.3–5.5 and Appendices D–G.

E5.justification: Figures 4–5 retain the same 95% confidence bands around fitted curves. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimation procedures, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the empirical figures retain their values and trends, including appendix results. For example, the minimum compression ratio remains 0.008, and Table 2 retains batch-512 latencies of 32.991 ms for KV caching and 0.695 ms for CollectiveKV.

T1.justification: The similarity and SVD definitions, projection and routing equations, loss definitions, and latency analysis in Equations 1–12 are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the same contributions: cross-user KV sharing, compression to 0.8% of original cache size, reduced latency, and maintained or improved recommendation performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of information sharing, pool capacity, router behavior, and long-tail performance are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitation concerning selection of the user-specific KV dimension and the proposed adaptive-selection direction.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly discloses reuse of FuxiCTR implementations and experimental infrastructure, and LAIN's splitting/configuration protocol. Appendix B replaces the anonymous repository pointer with a named CollectiveKV GitHub repository. Appendix C's hyperparameters and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds LAIN, BlossomRec, MALLOC, and two Zhu et al. benchmarking references from 2021 and 2022. These provide context and credit reused infrastructure and protocols; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief provenance statements and an acknowledgments section, updates affiliations and repository wording, and expands the references. The scientific prose, section sequence, and appendix organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: The author block is compacted, allowing the introduction onto page 1. Figures 1–2 occupy separate pages instead of sharing page 4, and text and float spacing shift elsewhere. The figures, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 5.1 and the new acknowledgments clarify and credit the reused codebase and experimental protocols, while Appendix B updates the code-access pointer. These modestly improve attribution and reproducibility documentation; the method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
